finding.claim: Path traversal / arbitrary file read in /dl. The user-controlled `f` query parameter is joined to the root with filepath.Join without any containment check. filepath.Join cleans `..` segments, so `../` sequences escape /srv/files and any file readable by the process is returned.
finding.source: HTTP GET /dl?f=<value> (files.go:12), unauthenticated, public listener on :8082 (files.go:34)
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: name := r.URL.Query().Get("f") takes attacker-controlled input with no validation
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") resolves to /etc/passwd; the result is passed to os.ReadFile
file contents are returned to the caller
handler registered on the default mux at /dl

finding.guards_checked: No authentication or authorization middleware. No filepath.Base, no prefix check after Clean, no os.Root or fs.ValidPath use, and no allowlist. Join's Clean does not prevent traversal, because it collapses `..` rather than rejecting it. No evidence of a reverse proxy that normalizes paths. Query-string values are URL-decoded by Go, so `..%2f` also works. The sibling /avatar handler (files.go:22) uses filepath.Base and is not vulnerable, which shows the safe pattern was not applied to /dl. Repro: curl 'http://host:8082/dl?f=../../etc/passwd'

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the unvalidated `f` query value to filepath.Join("/srv/files", name), which collapses `..` and lets it escape the root. The result goes to os.ReadFile and is written to the response at files.go:18, on an unauthenticated listener (files.go:32-34) with no containment check or auth.
